gates.title: Lock the research bet before I write the plan
gates.description: Three weeks with a part-time researcher buys one good study, not three. These answers decide what the method plan actually contains.

questions.label: Which bet should this study optimize for?
questions.description: Recommended: A. You are deciding whether to spend a quarter of engineering. That is expensive and slow to reverse, so a defensible answer on one narrow question beats a wide, thin map of the space.

options.label: Option A — Confidence, narrow scope (Recommended)
options.description: One question: will enough of these customers pay a recurring price for this? Priced concept test to both segments, a live behavioral signal, and pricing sensitivity. Produces a defensible go/no-go number. Tells you little about what the product should be.

options.label: Option B — Learning speed, broad exploration
options.description: Interviews across repeat and lapsed buyers on plant-buying rhythm, why lapsed buyers stopped, and what a subscription would have to do. Produces a strong product definition and a weak commercial number — the go/no-go stays a judgment call.

questions.label: How far can we go on a live willingness-to-pay test with real customers?
questions.description: Stated interest in subscriptions overstates real signup by a wide margin. Whatever you allow here sets the ceiling on how strong the evidence can be.

options.label: Real pre-sell — take a deposit or first payment, refundable
options.description: Strongest evidence. Also the highest brand risk if you then decide no-go, and it needs a refund and comms plan.

options.label: Priced waitlist — show real price and tiers, capture intent, no charge (Recommended)
options.description: Far stronger than a survey, buildable in days, low brand risk. Reserve-your-spot framing with an honest 'launching if there's demand' note.

options.label: Survey and interviews only — no live test
options.description: Fastest and safest, but the go/no-go rests on stated intent, which I will have to discount heavily in the brief.

questions.label: What existing data can the researcher pull without engineering help?
questions.description: Anything checked here becomes a zero-cost quant workstream — repeat rate, inter-order gap, category mix — instead of a question I have to spend incentive budget asking.

options.label: Order history per customer (dates, value, items)
Support tickets, reviews, or past customer messages
Site analytics (traffic, product page views, cart behavior)
None of it is accessible in three weeks
